environment: host ExUnit plus one disposable loopback PostgreSQL 16/17 fixture with synthetic keys/roles; no native/capture/phones

planned_commands.constructor: elixir selected pure modules and bounded fixture specs; exact command to be frozen with source ownership
planned_commands.catalog: selected standalone ExUnit current-catalog fixture through restricted LifecycleRepo; no broad harness
planned_commands.store: same bounded real PostgreSQL fixture with explicit barriers/fault injection
planned_commands.preauth: same fixture with real existing Vault and StoredSnapshot
planned_commands.attempt: same fixture plus fixed process owner and selected protocol modules
planned_commands.claim: selected ExUnit process-owner tests plus real durable claimed rows
planned_commands.identity: selected existing ordinary identity owner plus synthetic signed access token fixture
planned_commands.activate: same restricted-role fixture, real AEAD, default verifier and canonical SQL
planned_commands.uncertainty: bounded fault-injecting client/connection termination in owned fixture
planned_commands.logout: same fixture with concurrent canonical locks
planned_commands.workspace: later selected ordinary Endpoint/default verifier/default Repo fixture
planned_commands.provider: later separately selected fixed adapter tests; real provider remains external qualification
planned_commands.http: later selected real Endpoint/browser-protocol fixture; no UI automation
planned_commands.cleanup: fixture cleanup assertions plus owned process inventory
planned_commands.migration: bounded selected ordinary migration integration fixture

limitations: No command group is executed by this document-only slice.
Planned fixture commands must be concretely bound before their implementation run; this matrix is not execution evidence.
Synthetic provider/token/loopback TLS evidence is never real-provider, Neon, customer, FieldLog or GA qualification.
